neighbours.label: ' or' opening the second alternative of an embedded yes/no question ('if it is recyclable or not', 'whether X or Y'); the same slot is filled by Arabic 'am' and Chinese 'haishi' in the top examples
fire: The leaflet explains what each plastic is made from and if it is safe to reuse or not.
Before you buy, check whether the charger is included or not.
The nurse will ask if the pain is constant or not.
The survey records whether each household owns its home or rents it.
It does not matter to the tax office if the payment was made in cash or not.
Customs officers could not tell if the watches were genuine or not.
The judge has to consider whether the damage was caused on purpose or not.
Readers often wonder if the narrator is telling the truth or not.
quiet: The leaflet explains what each plastic is made from and how it can be reused.
Before you buy, check that the charger is included in the box.
The nurse will bring water or juice with the tablets.
The survey covers households that own their home and those that rent.
The tax office accepts payment in cash or by card at the counter.
Customs officers seized watches, rings or bracelets from three passengers.
The judge has to consider the damage that was caused on purpose.
Readers often enjoy a narrator who bends the truth a little.

notes: Card: ' or' x5, Arabic ' أم' x2, Chinese '还是', German clause-final verbs of indirect questions. Probes: 'if it is recyclable or not' 0.60, direct 'row-first or column-first?' 0.34, 'whether ... or' 0.11-0.26, list 'coffee or tea' 0.03, 'whether' without 'or' 0.03. An embedded 'when ... will be' scored 0.26, so the pole is wider than 'or' (indirect-question slot); the test stays on 'or'.
